notes.title: Set sail, strike a deal and rule the waves.

items.text: Dear Godir,

Set sail in search of endless wealth in the Age of Wonders 4: The Silver Seas expansion. Explore oceans rich with mystery, found Cities out on the open sea and cut deals that always leave you richer as the Mercantile Culture. Rule your empire with the alien beauty of the Aqualon and the monstrous might of the Sharkkin, strike a bargain with the Free Captains that prowl the seas and become the undisputed ruler of the waves.

Riding in on the tide is the Manta Update. This Free Update, available to all owners of Age of Wonders 4, brings Trade Routes, a brand new economic system that connects your Cities to Outposts, Free Cities and Empires beyond your borders. Water has been improved from the ground up, with cheaper embarking, Outposts on the waves, new rules for ships in combat and a visual overhaul of ocean combat maps, while Magic Fighters get a new Sword & Staff loadout.
The Silver Seas Expansion
Manta Update overview
Play Age of Wonders 4 for free this weekend
Bundles Update
The Silver Seas Art Blast
Post-Release Dev Stream
[dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eO9a8VNmosA"]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/5094370/Age_of_Wonders_4_The_Silver_Seas/"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/a4e736c079075b84face27f5227a1d71817975b6.png"]New Forms: Aqualon & Sharkkin

Two new Forms rise from the depths. The Aqualon are a graceful and aspirational people, near-human in shape with an alien, aquatic flair. The Sharkkin are their monstrous counterpoint: a powerful, martial Form that stands shoulder to shoulder with Orcs and Ogres, with a glint of teeth in every grin. Customize your faction with a variety of striking looks and create a unique character to rule the seas.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/ae527b7bfe35f418a499aed5f964e2fc2104bbcf.png"]New Culture: Mercantile

Become the Mercantile, a culture that always gets more out of a deal than the other side. They found Cities on Ocean and land alike, strike Trade Routes with any Free City that isn’t hostile, and fight dirty on the battlefield to gain an unfair advantage. Choose between two Organisations that define how your empire does business:
The Cartel (Shadow & Chaos) deals in information and manipulation, with camouflaged Smuggling Routes that reach even hostile Cities and Leverage that makes flanking attacks all the more deadly.

The Barony (Shadow & Materium) are wealthy trade princes backed by mercenary armies, with larger Outposts, extra Trade Routes per Vassal and Bounties that set their Bounty Hunters loose on targets of import.
Both bring their own City Structures, spells and a unique unit lineup, from the Informant and Envoy scouts to the Mageslayer and Silvershot.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/c3dbbc0b8dab1caf123fa0d4845f899dd9eccd35.png"]New Tomes

The Silver Seas contains 4 new Tomes drawn from the tides. Bend the currents to your will with the Tome of Hydromancy. Drag the cursed dead back up from the depths with the Tome of the Damned and its wailing Accursed Lamenter. Let Swashbucklers and Powder Keg Diplomacy do the talking in the Tome of Piracy, and when all else fails, freeze the world solid with the Tome of Eternal Ice and its Ancient Hoarfrost Manta.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video \/Video \
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/65480623d759892f400333f2c54215309f9afd2d.png"]New Dwelling: Bond of Free Captains

Out on the open ocean the Free Captains keep their bases, their stolen loot and their plans for the next raid. Each Dwelling is home to an independent Pirate Captain with their own personality and agenda. Some are Bloodthirsty, some Avaricious and a few even Heroic, so you will want to deal with each of them in their own way. Earn their allegiance to become Life-Bound and gain access to their stolen treasures, Pirate technologies and units. Cross them, and their Raids will come for your Trade Routes, Provinces and undefended Cities.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/0f38aeea3a42bba851c46ba53d6e617a5135aba3.png"]New Content: Ocean Happenings

The sea is no longer passive geography. A new set of Ocean Happenings turns the waves into a dynamic environment full of events, interesting gameplay and economic rewards, inviting you to set sail and claim what the ocean has to offer before your rivals do. Most of these Happenings are a boon rather than a bane, so keep a fleet at the ready: the sea rewards those who answer its call.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/6ed348360eb93283e950f4f9efd7e56d7ce4082f.png"]New Content: Ocean Locations

The Silver Seas fills the Oceans with new Landmarks, Ancient Wonders, Infestations, Magic Materials and Wildlife. Brave the Tempestuous Vortex, where Rune Crabs slingshot armies across the sea at breakneck speed, then dive beneath it to salvage the sunken riches of Armada’s Fall. Claim the Pearltide Dome to arm yourself with Pearltide Bombs, or harvest the ghostfire-infused Pale Tidebloom that blooms along the coast.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
Even More Content
While we’re sure the above has you drooling like a Sharkkin at feeding time, there’s even more that you can enjoy. Further included in The Silver Seas Expansion are:
6 Achievements
3 New Music Tracks
4 New Premade Rulers including the Legacy Ruler Marinus
New Realm Template: Pirate Reefs & New Realm Traits
New Exotic Mount: Seamare Mounts
New Society Trait: Children of the Waves
New Pirate Interface Skin & Banner Emblems
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/1d90d7735370fa0d1e0aea47a4b996bf27b77b68.png"]
Trade Routes

Trade Routes are a new economic system that connects your Cities to Outposts, Free Cities and the Cities of other Empires. Each Route is built and owned by a single City, and what you gain depends on what it connects to: Outposts funnel everything they produce into their City, Free Cities share their full output and can be steered with Trade Focuses, and a new Free Trade Agreement opens up trade with other Empires. New Trade structures let you specialize a City around its trade, and Routes can be raided in open war, paying out handsomely if you win.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/c22c910f85d62ce64de7de03901b74a421227e43.png"]Water Improvements

Water has always been something to cross rather than somewhere to be. The Manta Update changes that: embarking is cheaper, Outposts can be founded on Ocean waters to make better use of the seas around you, and abilities that summon, resurrect or teleport now work on the water, while embarked units follow their own rules for turning and positioning. Every ship now reflects the Faction that sails it, with three new Boat Skins to pick during Creation, new attack animations and Unit Enchantment visuals, all on ocean battle maps redressed with corals, kelp and sea life.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/378aa9fba8e69faa761a6c00763fcabf242b0cc0.png"]Spellblade Update

Magic Fighters receive a new weapon of choice: the Sword & Staff. Available as a Hero Loadout and in the Item Forge, it grants a Magic Strike main attack and a Dart secondary, with access to both Staff and Melee Infusions. The Spellblade and Death Knight classes have been updated to match.
Learn More: Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/c45dd77d09ddd7e9174af590296e87fd36057277.png"]
Quality of Life and more

For each Major Update we don’t just work on new Content, Balance Changes or Fixes. We always try to dedicate some time to improvements that make the game easier or more accessible to use. With the Manta Update we have a brand new set of Quality of Life Improvements for you to enjoy.
A new Chilled Status Effect joins the fray as the frosty counterpart to Burning, stacking up to 5 times before freezing its target solid, and has been woven into every icy corner of the game.
The Elder Vampire and Giant Kings have received a fresh round of updates, alongside a large balance pass over Tomes and Premade Item Equipment.

The battlefield is easier to read than ever: Unit abilities now show the turns remaining on their cooldown, and every combat screen names the battle being fought, so you always know what is at stake. In Faction Creation, five new Hunter Form Traits grant your people camouflage and Very Fast Movement on their home terrain, from Ashlands and Forests to Sand, Snow and Water.
We’ve also made a number of improvements to the Multiplayer session browser and connection handling.
This only skims the surface of the Manta Update. For the full list of change notes, please visit:
Read the full patch notes here

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/2d2c48116806f372ec738b95b0517b94317f49fb.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/50e2d70ddb5c0f66d97ba5a2b95b9942581aae67.gif"]
Water Improvements
Water has long been the least rewarding part of the map: costly to enter, limiting in combat, and visually flat. This update takes on all three, on the world map, in battle and on screen.
World Map Gameplay
Embarking now has a flat cost, Outposts can be founded on water provinces, and the Random Map Generator has been retuned so oceans shape the layout of a realm.
Movement & Settlement
Renamed terrain types: Ocean is now Deep Ocean, Coastal is now Ocean and Water is now Underground Water.
Changed the cost of embarking a unit from all of its Movement Points (minimum 12) to a flat 20 Movement Points.
Added the same +2 Vision granted to Embarked Units to Aquatic Units.
Added founding Outposts on habitable provinces with water in the center. These Outposts cannot be converted into Cities, except by the Mercantile Culture.
Added building the Spelljammer, Beacon of Unity and Teleporter Special Province Improvements on water provinces.
Random Map Generator
Continents
Increased ocean size and made continents more consistent in size, so the sea plays a bigger role in how a realm is laid out.
Changed continents belonging to AI players so they can connect to each other by land, instead of always being separated by water.
Changed AI players to no longer be placed on a shared continent with another player by default. Human players still start on a shared continent so they can reach each other early.
Coastal: Changed the ocean to sit in one corner of the map instead of being spread around the edges, with fewer and smaller islands.
Divide: Removed the islands along the ocean that splits the two continents, and increased the width of that ocean considerably, so it reads as a proper ocean rather than a wide river.
Islands
Removed the Lava terrain overlay, removing unsightly lava/ocean borders.
Changed resource values: lower on land, higher on the ocean.
Combat Gameplay
Embarked units follow their own rules for turning and positioning, with stats adjusted to match, and summons, resurrections, transformations and teleports now work at sea.
Embarked
Added Large Target and Reinforced.
Added -2 Fire Protection.
Removed -2 Defense and -2 Resistance.
Removed the damage reduction due to casualties.
Added Limited Maneuverability to embarked units, Ghost Ships and Ironclads:
Units spend Movement Points each time they turn while moving.
Using the Rotate Unit Ability spends all of the unit's remaining Movement Points.
Units cannot use Opportunity Attacks or Retaliations against hexes behind them.
Added Amphibious Movement to Ironclads.
Abilities & Spells on Water

Added the Water Walk passive, which is granted in combat to any unit that cannot cross the current map's terrain on its own (for example a land unit summoned on a water map), allowing it to use land movement on water hexes.
Changed abilities and spells that summon, resurrect or transform units to work on water maps (with a few rare exceptions, mostly involving plants).
Changed magical teleport abilities (e.g. Teleportation) to work on water.
Changed non-magical teleport abilities (e.g. Disengage Unit) to only be blocked while the unit is embarked.
Changed Amphibious units to become Wet while on water.
Visual Improvements

Water rendering has been reworked for readability, every aquatic battle map has been redressed with new props and sea life, and ships now carry the look of the culture that sails them, with new skins in Faction Creation.
Ship Customization
Added 3 unique Boat Skins to choose from during Faction Creation: Default, Graceful and Brutal.
Added a default ship style for each culture.
Changed Free Cities to use the ships of their associated faction, Dwellings to use their own boats where available, and other independents to use Marauder ships.
Added miniature boats to the Race Customization screen.
Updated ship animations, including run, turn, ability and spell-casting animations.
Added Unit Enchantment visuals on boats where applicable.
Water Rendering
Updated the ocean water visuals for better readability on water maps.
Added tactical combat ocean transparency.
Changed water battle maps to pick their atmosphere (lighting and weather) dynamically instead of using a fixed one.
Added fitting ocean-floor rocks to underground water battles.
Combat Maps
Added new ocean battle map props: shells, pearls, corals and kelp.
Added a water grave marker visual.
Updated combat map dressing for all aquatic combat maps.
Changed props and obstacles, including grave markers, to bob and move with the waves.
Added fish and ambient sea life swimming on the water.
Changed spell and ability effects in water battles to play on the water surface, so they are clearly visible instead of being hidden beneath it.
Added a water-themed effect when units cast spells while standing in water.
Added water splash effects to ships with magical ranged attacks.
Magic Fighter Weapons
Added Sword and Staff Hero Loadouts.
Added Sword and Staff weapons to the Item Forge.
“Sword & Staff” Weapon have access to the following Infusions:
+1 Range
Magic Missile
Lightning Strike
Hindering Blizzard
Crushing Anguish
Finger of Death
Poison Darts
Sundering Curse
Flame Strike
Stunning Flash
Freezing Blast
Exposing Light
Wail of the Banshee
Life Steal
+1 Retaliation
Extra Retaliation Damage (20% / 40% / 60%)
Added a custom frontend pose for the Sword and Staff loadout.
Updated Spellblade skills so that Magic Strikes are treated like Melee Strikes.
Updated Death Knight skills so that Magic Strikes are treated like Melee Strikes.
Pantheon
Base Game
5 Item Forge Visualisations
Water Orb
Frozen Orb
Damned Saber and Staff
Trident polearm
Rapier and Pistol
3 Customization Sets
Bloodthirsty Pirate Set
Wooden Leg
Hook
Eyepatch
Pirate Hat (shared)
Pirate Hat + Crow
Avaricious Pirate Set
Wooden Leg
Hook
Eyepatch
Pirate Hat (shared)
Pirate Hat + Parrot
Heroic Pirate Set
Wooden Leg
Hook
Eyepatch
Pirate Hat (shared)
Pirate Hat + Macaw
Society Trait - Merchant State
+2 Trade Route Capacity per Vassal
+10 City Stability to Cities with an active Trade Route
+5 Imperium for each Trade Route to another Empire's City
Reduces the cost of Trade Routes by 30%
Cities cannot be founded or absorbed.
Banner Icon - Pirate
DLC Ruler Unlocks
2 Dragon Lord Items
Seamare Frills
Seamare Ornamentation
2 Giant King Items
Pirate Head
Pirate Body
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/886cb4b1562f92ed23f43555f4b804b5fbe6f1df.gif"]
Trade Routes

Trade Routes are a new economic system that connects your Cities to Outposts, Free Cities, and the Cities of other Empires. Each Route is built and owned by a single City, which receives the Route's income; what you gain depends on what the Route connects to. Routes can be raided in open war, and a new line of City structures lets you specialize a City around its trade.
General
Trade Routes are created from the Trade Route panel and are built through the Unit Production Queue.
A Trade Route's Draft cost depends on its target and distance.
Trade Route production can be hurried.
Creating a Trade Route requires the target City to have been explored.

notes.title: Trade Route capacity is per City

items.text: 1 Route by default.
+1 per core Trade structure (Trade Post, Trade Quarters, Trade Bazaar).
+1 from the Caravaneer's Guild.
+3 in every City when the Megacities realm trait is active, or when your faction has the Chosen Destroyers Society Trait.
Trade Routes are guarded by Trader Escorts. Escort strength depends on the City's Trade structures:
Base: 2× Tier 1.
Trade Post: 3× Tier 1, 1× Tier 2.
Trade Quarters: 3× Tier 1, 3× Tier 2.
Trade Bazaar: 1× Tier 1, 3× Tier 2, 2× Tier 3.
Trade Routes are automatically regenerated or destroyed when territory along their path changes owner. The City's owner receives a notification explaining what happened.
Trade Routes also regenerate automatically when a province along their path is terraformed.
Trade Routes that pass through territory the owner no longer has access to are rerouted.
Nomad Cities: Trade Routes are restored for free when the settler unpacks.
Province Improvement “Teleporter”
Changed Upkeep from a local Outpost upkeep to a global empire upkeep of 10 Mana, so it no longer interacts with Trade Route income.
Economy
Culture Trait “Tyrannical Exploitation” (Dark)
Reduced Bonus from 20% to 2% per allegiance, to account for the much larger income now gained from Vassals.
Changed to only apply to Vassal tribute when an active Trade Route to that Vassal exists.
Description - Updated to state the 2% bonus instead of the previous 20%.
Culture Trait “Potential of Growth” (Mystic) - Removed its effect on Outposts.
Culture Trait “Potential of Control” (Mystic) - Removed its effect on Outposts.
Empire Skill 9B “Absolute Loyalty” (Order) - Reduced the Income bonus from Supreme Vassalage from +40% to +20%.
Society Trait “Chosen Uniters” - Reduced Income Bonus from +30% to +10%.
Interface
Added a Trade Routes overlay toggle to the overview map.
Trade Routes are otherwise only visible when a City is selected, an army is standing on a Route, or the Economic Overview is open.
Trade Route income is listed under its own “Trade Route” entry in the City income overview.
Added Trade Route information to the Outpost panel, including whether a Trade Route is connected and, if so, to which City.
Added a combat preview for battles involving Trade Routes.
Added tooltips for Trade Routes, including while they are still in the production queue.
Notifications
Added a notification when a Trade Route is completed.
Added separate notifications, each with its own message and event icon, for when one of your Trade Routes is raided, removed or rerouted.
Added a Trade Route Income concept, linked from the Trade Route tutorial and the Trade Route concept.
City Structures

Three core Trade structures, unlocked by City tier, grow with the City. Each also offers a choice between two mutually exclusive sub-structures, so a City can lean toward Outposts and Free Cities or toward trade with other Empires.
Trade Post (Tier 2)
Requires Town Hall II.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +5 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Outpost Supply Hub
Outposts connected to this City by Trade Route provide +50% income.
Diplomatic Embassy
Each Trade Route with another Empire's City grants this City +5 Imperium.
Trade Quarters (Tier 3)
Requires Trade Post.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +10 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Food Importers
Each Trade Route with an Outpost or Free City grants this City +20 Food and +10 Stability.
Wizard's Exchange
Each Trade Route with another Empire's City grants this City +10 Knowledge and +10 Mana.
Trade Bazaar (Tier 4)
Requires Trade Quarters.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +15 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Caravaneer's Guild
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Trade Routes cost 20% less Draft in this City.
Counts as a Guild; a City may only have one Guild.
Taxation Offices
Each Trade Route grants this City +5 Gold and +5 Stability.
Targets
Outposts
Outposts no longer have an economy of their own: a Trade Route makes an Outpost an extension of the connected City, sending everything its Domain produces there.
Outposts no longer cost 10 Gold upkeep.
Outposts provide no income until connected by a Trade Route.
An Outpost connected by a Trade Route sends all Local and Global income from its Domain to the connected City.
Each Outpost can only be connected to one City.
Outposts no longer receive Resource Sharing. This closes an exploit where Corrupt Pact would also grant its Food bonus to Outposts connected by a Trade Route.
Free Cities
Free Cities normally pay Tribute in Gold and Mana only. A Trade Route opens up their full output, Local resources included, and lets you steer what they produce through Trade Focuses.
A Trade Route can be established with any Free City you have at least a Pact of Cooperation with.
Base Free City Tribute (without a Trade Route) is capped at 10% of its Gold and Mana income.
Trade Route income from a Free City is a percentage of its income, set by your diplomatic state with it:
War: 5%
Pact of Cooperation: 5%
Pact of Loyalty: 10%
Establishing a Trade Route to a Free City grants +100 Relation with it.

notes.title: Trade Focuses replace the old Free City trade options

items.text: Available with any Free City you have a Trade Route with.
Costs Imperium per turn (5 at base) and lasts until cancelled.
Increases the Free City's output of the chosen resource by 50%, raising the income supplied through the Route.
Only one Focus can be active per Free City; the available options depend on the resources it produces.
Trade Focus treaties can be cancelled from the Diplomacy Overview screen.
Magic Material trades remain available.
Foreign Cities
With a Free Trade Agreement in place, two Empires can build Routes into each other's Cities.
Unlocked after a Wizard Bond.
While active, both Empires may build Trade Routes to each other's Cities.
Ending the agreement cancels all Routes between the two Empires.
A Trade Route to another Empire's City grants 20% of the target City's Gold and Mana income.
Raiding
Raiding is a wartime action: it requires a declared war, plays out as a full battle against the Route's Trader Escorts, and pays out well if you win.
Raiding requires being at war with the Route's owner. Attempting to raid without a war prompts you to declare one.
Raiding a Trade Route triggers a 1v1 battle against its Trader Escorts, with no reinforcements for either side. Surviving units keep any damage they took.
A successful raid grants a one-time reward of 3× the Route's per-turn income.
Routes destroyed when a City is occupied or conquered count as raided and grant raid income.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/bd446860bec4645b9964c59fee16899bcc0febf7.gif"]AI Difficulty - Removed the Gold and Mana income multipliers. These were only active on Normal Difficulty and above and only affected final income, not City income.
AI Turn Processing - Updated to reduce long AI turn times, particularly in late-game Classic mode games with many Trade Routes and events.
Combat AI
Increased the value of units with mind-control or summon abilities in combat AI evaluations.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/b10d26d53cbda44aff14c1c2f82b9765ef864661.gif"]
Added a proper defence animation to Guardians, so spears no longer clip through shields.
Updated the lighting on units shown in the frontend.
Added new tattoo customization options for Giant Lord rulers.

Added culture-specific world map visuals from Tier 1 for Barbarian and Primal culture cities: their own set of city props around the city center and a palisade wall around the settlement, instead of the generic Tier 1 city dressing.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/e7e3ae67d592a9702f923217d2ad47ae58306ebc.gif"]
The unit sustains a small amount of Frost damage each turn for 3 turns.
Stacks up to 5 times. At 5 stacks, Chilled is removed, the unit sustains a burst of Frost damage, and becomes Frozen for 1 turn.
Chilled is the opposing status effect of Burning.
Changed the effect inflicted when Frozen is resisted from Status Vulnerability to Chilled.
Added “Inflict Chilled” as an Item Forge Infusion.
General
Debuff “Blinded” - Reduced the number of Retaliations removed from all to 1.
Added the ability for Immobilized units to turn in place.
Removed the effect of Burning ground on Floating units.
Terrain Effect “Sunless” - Healing penalty in tactical combat - Reduced from -50% to -25%.
Changed the sun direction to flip when you are the defender in tactical combat, so battles are lit consistently for both sides.
Ability “Afflicting Miasma” - Added a chance to apply Chilled when dealing Frost damage.
Unit “Nomad Raider” - Added Demolisher to Fiery Momentum.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/6fe139167df1f1fe3c95431e0eadcbee1f1282f9.gif"]
Dark
Unit “Mortalist”
Ability “Death Hex”
Changed from Single Action to Full Action.
Increased Range from 4 to 6.
Removed Single Shot.
Increased Additional Targets from 1 to 2.
Note: this brings Death Hex in line with the other Tier 2 Battle Mage abilities.
Unit “Warlock”
Ability “Sundering Curse”
Removed Single Shot.
Increased Additional Targets from 1 to 2.
Industrious
Unit “Bastion”
Removed Single Shot from Defensive Sweep.
Increased Defensive Sweep Damage from 16 to 30.
Primal (Glacial Mammoth)
Status Effect “Fury of the Glacial Mammoth” - Changed from a 30% chance to inflict Frozen to a 60% chance to inflict Chilled.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/23ddafd61c609a73b7ae0c7f68e7f5436e859c68.gif"]
Materium

Skill 7 “Metropolitan Society” - Changed to affect the same set of income resources as Utopian Society: Added Imperium, Binding Essence, Binding Fragments, Astral Echoes, Wonderstone, Favors and War Spoils to the +10% bonus.
Nature
Skill 5B “Lasting Boons” - Changed to no longer extend positive status effects that cannot be dispelled, such as the effects Eldritch Sovereigns gain from Forbidden Tomes.
Order
Skill 9A “Utopian Society” - Changed to affect the same set of income resources as Metropolitan Society: Removed Happiness, Thralls and Embalmed Sacrifices from the +10% bonus.

releases.displayName: Announcing the Manta Update Open Beta

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/233b4672a38d8a64e4051a6a33e7e0d2763cf814.jpg"]
Hi all!

With The Silver Seas now announced, we can finally talk about everything coming with its Free Update. Starting now the Manta Update is in Open Beta for all Steam Users. Steam Owners of Age of Wonders 4 can access the Manta Update by opting into the manta_beta branch (see instructions below).

This beta brings the Water Improvements we've been working on for months: updated naval combat with abilities and spells that work at sea, ship customization, overhauled water visuals on the World Map and in Combat, and Outposts on water provinces. It also includes the new Trade Routes feature, which links your Cities to Outposts, Vassals and other Empires. Rounding out the Update are new Hero Loadouts, Form Traits, Ruler updates, Pantheon Content and more.

notes.title: With our Open Betas we set out for two things

items.text: A big benefit of our Open Betas is the incredible amount of Stability feedback we receive. What you’re receiving today is the version of the game we will be submitting for Certification. While this Open Beta is running we’re simultaneously developing our Day 1 Patch. Things might be a bit more hotcode but this allows us to address the most pressing issues for our Release Build.

We also want to give the Modding Community a headstart in updating their content to match the new update. We’ve done some testing to verify initial compatibility but there’s a vast variety of mods and mod combinations out there.
After updating to the Manta Beta your in-game version will read 1.017.00X.XXXXXX.

The most effective way to provide us with feedback is by making a Discussion Thread in the Open Beta Discussions. There’s a couple different types of Feedback that we can process during this Beta period.
Balance

With all of these changes there will naturally be a lot of Balance Feedback. Our goal is to address any extreme imbalances and important feedback that needs to be tackled for the Release. We only have time to make these changes until Thursday October 22nd.

Balance changes that require us to change text can be handled as long as they are made before Monday October 19th. Any text-involved balance requests after that as well as smaller balance concerns will be addressed during our regular development period as resources allow.
Stability
Crashes reported with the Crash Tool will automatically show up in our back end, so when you experience a crash please make sure to Upload those.
If you have a Blocker i.e. a Crash or Hang that will not allow you to continue your game, please make a report and include your Crash Report Name - given after upload - so we can tackle it.
Any general Bugs reported are welcome but not the main focus of this period, we’ll try to address those in a timely manner depending on our available resources.
Modding

If you experience issues and suspect that it might be related to one of the mods you have installed, then please verify which mod it may be by disabling your mods. If you’ve determined which Mod is causing your issue try to contact the Mod Developer first.
If you experience crashes with your mods, then please make a thread as stated above. While outdated mods can cause issues, we do try to ensure that they do not crash.
The Silver Seas Release
The final Update of this Beta will be when we submit the D1P for Certification. After that the branch will remain active until the release of The Silver Seas & the Manta Update on November 3rd.

When the time of release hits the Beta branch will be updated to include The Silver Seas Content, this ensures a smooth transition for users switching back to the Default branch. A few hours after release ~18 CET, the Manta Beta Branch will be disabled and removed. Any remaining users will be automatically moved back to Default when this occurs but it’s advised to switch back yourself after you’ve verified that you have access to The Silver Seas content on the Beta Branch.

notes.title: Getting into the Beta - What you need to know

items.text: If you want to take part in the beta there are a few important things you need to know!
This Beta is only available on Steam, owners on Console, Epic or Gog will receive the full Manta Update alongside The Silver Seas Expansion on November 3rd.
If a save has been made in Open Beta, there’s no going back! You will not be able to open that save in the game outside of the beta until the beta ends on November 3rd!

Spent Pantheon Points & Unlocked Content do not transfer between branches. If you unlock the new Pantheon Content included with the Manta Update during the Beta and decide to switch back your spent points will be lost. The Pantheon Content will need to be reacquired when returning to the beta branch or upon release.

Only use this in multiplayer if all participants agree. Make sure you do not use the beta in multiplayer without checking with the other players first, once a multiplayer game session has been updated to use the open beta, you cannot go back to previous versions!
To switch to a custom branch in the Steam client, right-click on the game from the library page and select "Properties".
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/84125cc3e31f12ad7f4ba921f49c4ee14d60fb5c.png"]
Among the available tabs will be the "Game Versions & Betas" tab.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/a5d0cf7db2fe6e0620aae3ee4a6034122a07cc0c.png"]
The Manta Beta should be listed in the dropdown menu under "Selected Game Version". A restart of your Steam Client may be needed if the Branch isn’t visible.

releases.displayName: Dev Diary #64 - Empire Tree Update

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/7b2b8d70d085ab20e90185de49e25059be2acaf5.jpg"]

Hey there, Emperors and Empresses! Welcome back to another Dev Diary. I’m Bas, senior game designer at Triumph Studios, and this time, I’ll be taking you through the rework of the Empire Development Tree—excitingly anticipated, a huge undertaking and, frankly, very scary! Let’s start at its very roots!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/bdb7390831215a0872f79ccc4e9a3aee469db0d9.png"]

notes.title: The Roots of the Tree (Design Origins)

items.text: In the early development stages of Age of Wonders 4, a need for a system arose that allowed players to represent the affinities of their empire in a more global way. We already had Tome Skills to add pieces on top of a player’s empire, but no real way to fully modify the general playstyle of an empire based on its affinities, especially on a strategic level.

Out came the first version of the Empire Development Tree. Each affinity had a skill path that would gradually unlock as the game progressed by accumulating affinity. The skills in each path would be designed to focus on strategic systems or mechanics that represented that affinity, such as pillaging for Chaos, spellcasting for Astral, diplomacy for Order, and so on.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/9ea50a33b2fa1caca31458a65e853027d6193fd5.png"]

Later on, Rites were added as fire and forget skills, mainly for the purpose of giving the players additional instant tools that fit the affinity, such as giving a specific resource or spawning a specific unit. In addition, the generic branch was added to add skills that didn’t necessarily fit into a single affinity and were more universally useful but had to be paced out.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/02641475b0e6f1722f2a9ed6a6048e39334cae78.png"]

The skills of the empire tree were unlocked by accumulating affinity points and spending imperium. Imperium was used as a secondary cost to make sure you don’t simply want to rush tomes for the sake of getting more affinity points and thereby unlock empire skills faster, giving research a sort of double purpose of progression.

And so there we were at release, with the Empire Development Tree defining certain playstyles for empires based on affinity! Some of the skills even became fan favorites, such as the diabolical Balor with Power From Slaughter.
Barking up the Right Tree (The Feedback)

The Empire Tree from release has seen several changes over the years. With certain skills being reworked, tweaked and some of its pacing altered. But over time, more pressing issues with the Tree’s overall design philosophy became apparent. The following 3 big points prompted us to look for a general review and rework of the Empire Tree:

First off, the Tree did not offer much in the way of choices once you went down an affinity path. You only had one line of skills to pick from per affinity branch. The only real choice you had was whether you were willing to pay the imperium for it. This wasn’t great, especially since the core pillars of Age of Wonders 4 were Player Expression and Replayability, both defined by meaningful choices the player can make during gameplay.

Secondly, we couldn’t fit the various niche identities of each affinity in the limited amount of skills each branch had. This meant some player fantasies associated with affinities couldn’t be fulfilled with the empire tree.
Thirdly, once you reached the end of a branch, that was it. There was no purpose for any excess imperium or affinity points. This was especially bad for mono-affinity empires.

Lastly, a design principle of the first iterations of the Empire Tree was to focus each affinity branch into particular resource types, such as Mana for Astral. This sounded good on paper, but as the game evolved, resource types shifted a lot in balance in relation to each other. This meant that certain Empire Development Tree branches became very strong or weak due to the resource type they focused on. Knowledge for Shadow was considered strong, while Food for Nature was considered weak.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/1c678a47f793aeef3ae58244dc00a2b6bcd9a015.png"]
As can be seen, there’s very few sources in Nature for resource types other than Food and Population.
Several key goals were established for a rework based on the previous feedback points:
Increase replay value by adding mutual exclusive choices
Add and rework existing skills to fulfil more player fantasies per affinity
Remove the extreme focus of one resource type per affinity branch
Make Rites repeating, so that accumulating affinity and imperium can be spent once a branch reaches the end.

These points sound simple, but this would be a huge undertaking as we also have to consider balance and the fact that we’d be putting some skills on the cutting block while some players may have appreciated them. It took various iterations and design discussions to come to a first version that we were comfortable enough to implement for testing.
Let’s go through the major steps that the design process took!
Pruning the Tree (Removing Skills)

One of the first steps to this new Tree was to look carefully at each existing skill and Rite and decide whether to cut it, or keep it either in its existing slot or moved around. The main criteria were:
Do we need and can we fill the space left behind if the skill was removed?
Does the skill fulfil the new design philosophy of the tree?
Certain skills or rites, like the formerly mentioned famous Balor with Power from Slaughter, were unfortunately cut due to no longer having a good place in the new Tree.

Especially unique unit unlocks were great for players that were going down a specific path, such as a demonic empire. But what about players that still wanted to tread the path of chaos without specifically going into demonology? Rites and Skills in the new Tree needed to be broad enough to fulfil multiple player fantasies, not just one.

So, the majority of skills were removed due to being too specific, making them irrelevant for some players but also feeling bad if you didn’t pick them. After all, even with the added mutual exclusivity, players don't have a lot of alternatives.
Worry not though, since for every slot opened, new skills and rites would be designed to fill them! So what was the process there?
Growing the Tree (Adding and Changing Skills)

As you might’ve noted in the image below, the new tree has a whopping 44 additional nodes in it. But that’s not even the total amount of skills or rites that were added or changed! These new or reworked skills were designed with varying purposes in mind, so that each skill was more widely applicable to player fantasies.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/daa4a77ce01f7115520535d03bb2fc2ea6dc3d17.png"]A glimpse of the design board of the new Empire Tree during development

Some examples are the various Infrastructure skills, present in all affinity branches. They grant discounts to structures that provide specific types of income. It doesn’t matter if you’re a druidic, bestial or floral kind of nature empire, the skill remains relevant.

We have still retained or created new more complicated skills. Especially where we felt like particular player experiences related to affinities couldn’t be fulfilled via tome skills, but were sought after regardless. These often come paired with a more straightforward skill, to offer a generic alternative to a more niche skill.

For example, Cultural Exchangers in the Order Branch grants Knowledge for each treaty you have. This opens up an avenue of faster research and a focus on diplomacy for an Order Empire, but it relies on friendly empires and free cities being around. So it is paired with the more universally applicable Spiritual Conviction, which provides mana for maintaining stable cities.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/81c6c862c7a5ec4404612e7074d2af837b28c74d.png"]

For Rites, we’ve either changed or updated all of them to become repeatable! Each Rite increases in Imperium cost and affinity point requirement per use. This meant some more unique rites were once again reworked into something more universal, such as the famous Breastplate of the Champion rite in Materium instead granting Essence and Fragments for the Item Forge (I’m sure someone will argue that they do in fact want 5x Breastplates of the Champion).
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/dd2abeec833f565223e9707911a71f81f51511e5.png"]
Rite of Swift Shadows can be used multiple times in a playthrough to launch sudden offenses or retreat your armies out of vulnerable positions.
Long Live the New Tree (The End Result)

This was not a one and done kind of process, in fact, there is still iteration to be done. Theorizing and creating formulas to calculate value is something us Game Designers do to help with creating content, but a lot also comes down to feeling and interpretation, since the Empire Tree lives in an everchanging context. It was honestly a very daunting task to have done this rework and some people may notice they miss some old skills.

But in the end we landed on a tree that we feel is more expansive, allows for more replayability and more widely supports the player fantasies each affinity can represent. It is a tree you can build your empire on. And so we hope you’ll have a great time exploring all the new options and builds available in the free update that came alongside Secrets of the Archmages!
PS: a huge shoutout to our 2D artists, who have made a boatload of new icons for the new and changed skills and rites!
Until next time, mighty Empire builders!

notes.title: Take a walk down memory lane

items.text: Unravel the Hidden Powers of the Cosmos in the Age of Wonders 4: Secrets of the Archmages Story Pack. Follow the footsteps of Athla’s renowned Wizard Kings through Tomes and Story Realms. Discover the Shrouded Isles they created, the Secret Arts they learned, and face the perils left in their wake as they ventured through the most infamous Worlds of the Astral Sea.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3976910/Age_of_Wonders_4_Secrets_of_the_Archmages/"]Guiding you on this nostalgic journey is the Sprite Update. This Free Update, available to all owners of Age of Wonders 4, brings a rework of the Reaver Culture, which introduces two Subcultures as Governments. A revamp of the Empire Development Tree brings new opportunities for expression of your faction identity, and a variety of Updated Settings, new cosmetics, and Faction Creation options bring you more of what you already love.
Check below for all the details on the Secrets of the Archmages Story Pack and the Sprite Update.

notes.title: Secrets of the Archmages Story Pack

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/ebe4e0f03c0446adf16178fd4e7a7edcade73c64.png"]
New Story: Circles of Power

Follow the footsteps of Athla’s renowned Wizard Kings. Accompany Merlin on his return to Evermore, where they comb through the secrets left behind by the Wizard Kings of the crumbled Circle of Deogai. On the Azh’Ruun Pit, the player encounters the target of Karissa’s unleashed fury: an ancient Circle of Deogai, teetering on collapse. Venture to the Burrow Downs on the fey world Duatha, learn to navigate and understand a realm of constant change and trickery, or Ham Binger will be lost!
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/f083912c8021f13a9257754a1eaefc773e71b91f.png"]
New Form: Owlkin

The Owlkin embody quiet wisdom and subtle presence; wise and watchful beings associated with secrets and knowledge. They feel set apart from their kin, carrying an air of mystery without losing their grounded nature. Customize your faction with a variety of striking looks and create a unique character to rule.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/fdac42288241df93633f88e1bb024ec74492a860.png"]
New Tomes

Secrets of the Archamages contains 6 new Tomes, each themed around a Wizard King featured in the Story Realms. Follow in the footsteps of Merlin with the Tome of Abjuration & Tome of the Cosmos; embrace the Chaos like Karissa with the Tome of Gluttony & Tome of Burning Passion; make harrowing escapes like the famed explorer Ham Binger with the Tome of Sprite, and creep along the shadows like the Spider Queen Arachna with the Tome of the Weaver.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Part 1, Part 2
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/ab4df22600d4221671c96e641f2abdc9d108d1f3.png"]
New Layer: Shrouded Isles & Secrets Spells

Shrouded Isles are “pocket dimensions”, small islands surrounded by an impenetrable void that have been created by wizards in ages past to guard their most powerful secrets, concealed from the eyes of the Archons. In these Shrouded Isles, you can explore unique environments, learn about the Godir who created them, and eventually claim these powerful secrets for yourself.

Secret Spells are more powerful or weird than normal spells, which would not appear in normal Tomes. When winning a realm while in possession of a Secret Spell artifact, the Godir can keep the spell as an Ascension Trait, instead of taking a trait from one of their Tomes.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/267abbf563e1d3080da562f07c13e5a82faee9db.png"]
New Content: Landmarks & Infestation

As the mysteries surrounding the Circles of Deogai are revealed, so are the things they kept hidden. Modified versions of the major Landmarks featured during the Story Realms can be encountered on your Custom Realms. Claim the Broken Wizard’s Throne, appease the Chained Hellion, or frolic in the Mistflow Gardens. The world is not without peril, though, as the Mistwalkers are expanding beyond the boundaries of Duatha and establishing Mistwalker Camp Infestations.
Even More Content
While we’re sure the above has your mouth watering, there’s even more that you can enjoy. Further included in the Secrets of the Archmages Story Pack are:
8 Achievements
5 New Music Tracks
2 New Premade Rulers
New Realm Templates & Realm Traits
Weaver Spider Mounts
New Secrets of the Archmages Interface Skin & Banner Emblems
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/faec44f14756a6a546b16e3a8c8f7e639f0ac5d9.png"]
Reaver Governments

The Reavers were our first DLC Culture, closing out 2023 with the Empires & Ashes Expansion. Since then, we’ve introduced the concept of Sub Cultures and generally improved our Culture Designs. The Reaver's World Map Gameplay has had a problem of being too restricted and narrow, impacting diplomatic gameplay much more harshly than intended. With the Reaver Governments, we are making them much more two-dimensional and bringing them up to snuff.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/42d29c233dfa3a8ba04ded28a9dc0bfd89e86f74.png"]
Empire Development Tree Update

The Empire Development Tree has been updated and significantly expanded. Over time, the way that the tree was originally designed no longer matches the way that the game has evolved. Empire Skills now represent a broader interpretation of their affinities and provide a better expression of your faction.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/b14ebed46ca49ee39531da95b120a07f710abede.png"]
Teams Update

Teams have always been about providing an easy way to work together towards Victory, without having to go through the various Diplomatic Requirements to establish an Alliance. However, this also meant all Diplomacy between individual Teams would be turned off. With the Teams Update, we’re adding two new settings that will allow you to team up at game start, without losing out on diplomatic intricacies.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/4cf4738b7b6e8ac93aa65c19575156321fe4d626.png"]
Quality of Life and more

For each Major Update, we don’t just work on new Content, Balance Changes, or Fixes. We always try to dedicate some time to improvements that make the game easier, more accessible to use, or simply more enjoyable.

With the brand new Narrative Content Filter, you gain additional control over what kind of Narrative Content can appear during a game. Replacing some of our older Realm Traits, you can now adjust the probability and presence of various Happenings, Lost Souls, and Wandering Merchants. We’ve also expanded Customization Options with brand new Wizard King Outfits based on recognizable Tome Units, Magic Wielders have access to a new Class of Weapons called Grimoires, and your faction can now ride more beasties into Combat.
This has only slightly lifted the veil on the Sprite Update. For the full list of change notes, please visit:
Sprite Update Patch Notes

releases.displayName: Announcing the Sprite Update Open Beta

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/9e577a9ea56ef6bf6605939b554917f2e68c3e65.png"]
Hi all!

Now that the Secrets of the Archmages are slowly being revealed and we can finally talk about all the exciting things coming with the Free Update. Starting now the Sprite Update is in Open Beta for all Steam Users. Steam Owners of Age of Wonders 4 can access the Sprite Update by opting into the sprite_beta branch (see instructions below). This beta contains the long awaited Empire Development Tree Update, nearly doubling the Tree in size. For owners of Empires & Ashes, this update also contains the surprise Reaver Culture Rework. But that’s not all, we have the new Narrative Content Filters as well as a Teams Update that will give more flexibility to your game starts.

notes.title: With our Open Beta’s we set out for two things

items.text: A big benefit of our Open Betas is the incredible amount of Stability feedback we receive. What you’re receiving today is the version of the game we will be submitting for Certification. While this Open Beta is running we’re simultaneously developing our Day 0 Patch. Things might be a bit more hotcode but this allows us to address the most pressing issues for our Release Build.

We also want to give the Modding Community a headstart in updating their content to match the new update. We’ve done some testing to verify initial compatibility but there’s a vast variety of mods and mod combinations out there.
After updating to the Sprite Beta your in-game version will read 1.015.000.121941.

The most effective way to provide us with feedback is by making a Discussion Thread in the Open Beta Discussions. There’s a couple different types of Feedback that we can process during this Beta period.
Balance

With all of these changes there will naturally be a lot of Balance Feedback. Our goal is to address any extreme imbalances and important feedback that needs to be tackled for the Release. We only have time to make these changes until Friday June 5th.

Balance changes that require us to change text can be handled as long as they are made before June 1st. Any text-involved balance change as well as smaller balance concerns will be addressed during our regular development period as resources allow.
Stability
Crashes reported with the Crash Tool will automatically show up in our back end, so when you experience a crash please make sure to Upload those.
If you have a Blocker i.e. a Crash or Hang that will not allow you to continue your game, please make a report and include your Crash Report Name - given after upload - so we can tackle it.
Any general Bugs reported are welcome but not the main focus of this period, we’ll try to address those in a timely manner depending on our available resources.
Modding

If you experience issues and suspect that it might be related to one of the mods you have installed, then please verify which mod it may be by disabling your mods. If you’ve determined which Mod is causing your issue try to contact the Mod Developer first.
If you experience crashes with your mods, then please make a thread as stated above. While outdated mods can cause issues, we do try to ensure that they do not crash.
Secrets of the Archmages Release

The final Update of this Beta will be when we submit the D0P for Certification. After that the branch will remain active until the release of Secrets of the Archmages & the Sprite Update on June 16th.

When the time of release hits the Beta branch will be updated to include the Secrets of the Archmages Content, this ensures a smooth transition for users switching back to the Default branch. A few hours after release ~18 CEST, the Sprite Beta Branch will be disabled and removed. Any remaining users will be automatically moved back to Default when this occurs but it’s advised to switch back yourself after you’ve verified that you have access to the Secrets of the Archmages content on the Beta Branch.

notes.title: Getting into the Beta - What you need to know

items.text: If you want to take part in the beta there are a few important things you need to know!
This Beta is only available on Steam, owners on Console, Epic or Gog will receive the full Sprite Update alongside the Secrets of the Archmages Story Pack on June 16th.
If a save has been made in Open Beta, there’s no going back! You will not be able to open that save in the game outside of the beta until the beta ends on June 16th!

Spent Pantheon Points & Unlocked Content do not transfer between branches. If you unlock the new Pantheon Content included with the Sprite Update during the Beta and decide to switch back your spent points will be lost. The Pantheon Content will need to be reacquired when returning to the beta branch or upon release.

Only use this in multiplayer if all participants agree. Make sure you do not use the beta in multiplayer without checking with the other players first, once a multiplayer game session has been updated to use the open beta, you cannot go back to previous versions!
To switch to a custom branch in the Steam client, right-click on the game from the library page and select "Properties".
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/84125cc3e31f12ad7f4ba921f49c4ee14d60fb5c.png"]
Among the available tabs will be the "Game Versions & Betas" tab.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/a5d0cf7db2fe6e0620aae3ee4a6034122a07cc0c.png"]
The Sprite Beta should be listed in the dropdown menu under "Selected Game Version" A restart of your Steam Client may be needed if the Branch isn’t visible.
Check out the full list of changes included in the Sprite Update here

releases.displayName: Rise from Ruin and Scorpion Update Out Now!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/2dfc3ed063b18a108f265da71fd2b4d2a8c0885f.jpg"]
Be Rude and become the Sandstorm that conquers the wastes.

Forge a mighty realm from the ashes in the Age of Wonders 4: Rise from Ruin Culture Pack. Journey into the Withered Worlds and explore their devastated landscapes with the Nomad Culture, uniquely adapted to survive and thrive in desolation. Lead a nation of Harefolk, survivors who outran the apocalypse itself as you Unearth the lost magics that ravaged these realms.

Hidden amongst the lost treasures of the Realms is the Scorpion Update. This Free Update, available to all owners of Age of Wonders 4, is sure to shake up your adventures. Before you set foot on a new Realm you can make use of the full spectrum of Colors with the new Color Picker. Once you do cross that portal navigating rebalanced Units, a new Unit Class/Role/Type and an updated Experience Scale will leave your games feeling new and yet the same in all the best ways.
Check below for all the details on the Rise from Ruin Culture Pack and the Scorpion Update.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/f088c5407e7d718001db9b78dd04d6c9742d5c13.png"]
New Form: Harefolk

Stepping into the Harefolk Form means becoming one of the cataclysm’s quickest survivors. These folks aren’t soft or cute; they’re sharp-eared scavengers who slipped through the world’s collapse with speed, instinct, and a stubborn will to live. Now they haunt the ruins, darting through broken Cities and outsmarting whatever still stalks the Withered Worlds.
Learn More: Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/03e21922f2fd18a43c5268637b3afda488d76735.png"]
New Culture: Nomads

Become the Nomads, masters of mobility on the battlefield and world alike, carrying entire cities across the realm in relentless pursuit of conquest and power. Representing the scavengers of the magical wastes as well as conquering hordes, they seek locations of interest, rapidly extracting exceptional value before leaving it barren and moving to a new location.
Nomads cities can be relocated by packing up and traveling to a new location to settle, maintaining all their upgrades and population.
Nomad cities “Overharvest” nodes in their domain, destroying them and gaining an “Essence” of that node in return.
Nomads can quickly rearrange the provinces in their city with little friction, allowing them to quickly reconfigure their cities to match their requirements.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/141bf8d180d4dd7d227f9751d61ae012c8613f4d.png"]
New Tomes

To conquer the frontier, you must see the desolation not as an obstacle, but as a crucible. True mastery of this harsh environment lies beyond mere survival; it is found in your capacity to strategically mold the hostile landscape to your command. Whether you are forging an empire of iron or commanding the shifting dunes, these tomes provide the ultimate blueprint for mastering the wastes.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/afa6e996ed56aac40fe2b08b4e05869cae69e91d.png"]
New Fated Regions: Echoes of the Fracturing (& Crisis)

A new realm trait, Echoes of the Fracturing, introduces a new set of Fated Regions. In a distant age ambitious Archmages experimented with the very essence of mana. They sought to obtain the power of the Well of Creation, yet the results of their efforts were devastating.The Devouring Winds are a wind-born hunger that absorbs all the magic out of everything and mutates it. Leaving the eroded Astral Barrens in its wake and its mana-starved beasts hunt for the last remains of magic.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/ba1da5c43874a0b9705261f6bbcb7bfbfd86ce3a.png"]
New World Map Content: Barren Regions & Ruined Wonders

Barren Regions are a new group of Handcrafted Regions that make use of the new Astral Barrens terrain. Within this terrain Magic-origin units cannot regenerate health, and all province mana generation is disabled. Even more so any spells cast within these borders risk backfiring. One might even find a Ruined Ancient Wonder… These are once-mighty structures turned into hollow monuments of a Realm scarred by magical fallout. A few iconic Wonders have been fully reimagined to embody this desolation more vividly.
Learn More: Dev Diary & Video
Even More Content
While we’re sure the above has your mouths watering, there’s even more that you can enjoy. Further included in the Rise from Ruin Culture Pack are:
6 Achievements
3 New Music Tracks
3 New Premade Rulers
New Realm Templates & Realm Traits
Camel & Scorpion Mounts
New Rise from Ruins Interface Skin & Banner Emblems
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3976900/Age_of_Wonders_4_Rise_from_Ruin/"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/47ace4677d4f8e49fc59b4e20010893fc46ca832.png"]
Gameplay Updates
Some big chances are coming in the Scorpion Update.
Move Speed Normalization

All regular units now share the same number of Move Points on the World Map. This ensures that mixing slower and faster units in a single army no longer reduces the overall travel speed, allowing for higher army diversity and strategy.
Defense & Resistance

We’re updating how Defense and Resistance work across all units to bring them back in line with their original design intent. The new system changes how damage reduction is applied, focusing on the source of damage rather than the type of damage dealt.
Experience

All units now gain XP automatically each turn, even when not fighting. This means your armies will continue to improve simply by existing and participating in your empire. XP gained from battles has been halved which means Units still get rewarded for combat, but fighting is no longer the only reliable way to level up.
Learn More: Dev Diary
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/764053b77bae896c32314aa2057335115c81edf6.png"]
Color Picker

This new Customization feature puts the colors of the rainbow at your finger tips. Simply select the Custom Color Icon at the end of the available Swatches or switch to the Custom Color Tab. Pick the exact color you want using Color Space & Hue Sliders, RGB Sliders or Hex Values. The Color Picker is available for the Banner, Skin Color, Hair Color, Armor Color and Metal Color.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/36f4bf6db30c0cd43cc9d00d4c9778d3c69c64fe.png"]
Quality of Life and more

For each Major Update we don’t just work on new Content, Balance Changes or Fixes. We always try to dedicate some time to improvements that make the game easier or more accessible to use. With the Scorpion Update we have a brand new set of Quality of Life Improvements for you to enjoy.

Transferring & Capturing Provinces has a new and improved User Flow. Now using the Province Pins it will be easier to see which Provinces are available and who owns them. Acquire Provinces from Vassal Cities for a small Imperium Cost or Capture Pillaged Provinces and instantly convert them to a Province Type of your choice.
The Item Forge has been updated to allow Defense Mode Infusions on Shields. Alongside the default Defense Mode they can now be forged with Defense Mode: Protective Wall or Defense Mode: Stone Wall.

We’ve done a pass to adjust some of the inconsistencies between the various Cultures. All Culture Enchantments will now apply to Mythic Units, the income of their replacement City Structure have all been matched up and a Structure Costs have been fixed. Don’t forget to check out the Primal Culture, which has received tons of love on top of this.
There’s more than just these Highlights when it comes to the Scorpion Update. For the full list of change notes
The Scorpion Update Patch Notes

As usual, once you enjoyed the Rise from Ruin and new Scorpion Update, feel free to join us for the Post-release Dev Stream on our YouTube at 14:00 CET on Thursday March the 12th and share your feedback!
Watch the stream on Thursday!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/e04b1812e019f05cc994f8e4c4eb7f5686b46323.png"]
Hello everyone!
Rise from Ruin and the accompanying Scorpion update are coming in less than a week - next Monday, 9th of March! Read the patch notes to find out what is to come:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/50e2d70ddb5c0f66d97ba5a2b95b9942581aae67.gif"]
Move Speed Normalization

All regular units now share the same number of Move Points on the World Map. This ensures that mixing slower and faster units in a single army no longer reduces the overall travel speed, allowing for higher army diversity and strategy.
All units now have 40 Move Points on the World Map
All Scout Units now have 48 Move Points on the World Map
Added Combat Speed, a new stat that indicates how many hexes per turn a unit can move in Combat.
Changed the rounding on the Combat Speed to Action Point Calculation. In most cases you will now have more action points when moving the same distance in pre-Scorpion.
Associated Updates
Form “Feline” - Now also has Elusive
Form “Lupine” - Now also has Ferocious
Form Trait “Athletics”

Defense/Resistance Update

We’re updating how Defense and Resistance work across all units to bring them back in line with their original design intent. The new system changes how damage reduction is applied, focusing on the source of damage rather than the type of damage dealt. We’re also adding a new Unit Role that deals Magic Damage at Melee range, the Magic Fighter.
The Defense stat now reduces all Damage (including Magic Damage) from Abilities that have Melee or Physical Ranged tags
The Resistance stat now reduces all Damage (including Physical Damage) from Abilities that have the Magic tag and Spells
In the case that an attack would be blocked by both Defense and Resistance, the higher value is chosen.
Renamed Damage Channel Resistance to Damage Channel Protection
Damage Channel Protection is added to Defense or Resistance to determine final Damage Reduction
Added Damage Channel Protection: Physical
Rebalanced the stats of the core unit types - Most units have less resistance than defense, with exceptions for battle mages, support units and ranged units which have more resistance than defense.
Ability descriptors like Magic and Base now have tooltips that explain what they mean
New Unit Role: Magic Fighter
Uses Melee Range attacks that count as Magical called Magic Strike.
Have the Passive “Melee Mage” allowing for Ranged Magic Attacks to be used when engaged
Uses most Battle Mage Unit Enchantments and the defensive or generic Fighter Unit Enchantments.

All units now gain XP automatically each turn, even when not fighting. This means your armies will continue to improve simply by existing and participating in your empire. releases.displayName: Announcing the Scorpion Update Open Beta

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/e04b1812e019f05cc994f8e4c4eb7f5686b46323.png"]
Hi all!

The release of Rise from Ruin is slowly approaching and as with every release it’s accompanied by a Free Update. Starting now the Scorpion Update is in Open Beta on Steam. Steam Owners of Age of Wonders 4 can access the Scorpion Update by opting into the scorpion_beta branch (see instructions below).

When you enter this Beta you’ll encounter a massively different Age of Wonders 4. Over the past few months we’ve spent a lot of effort revamping some of the core military systems. The goal of these changes is to address some of the larger balance and QoL issues that are inherent to the current system.
Move Speed Normalization

Movement Speed has a huge influence on early-game pacing and success. Previously, armies with faster units could reach more battles, gain more resources, and snowball into stronger positions. Because an army moves at the speed of its slowest unit this created a preference for Mounted Traits and Fast moving Units, limiting army diversity and strategy.

All regular units now share the same number of Move Points on the World Map. This ensures that mixing slower and faster units in a single army no longer reduces the overall travel speed. Scouts retain their 48 Move Points, maintaining their role as fast and exploratory units. To reflect the impact of all these changes we’ve rebalanced the costs and effects of various Movement and Mount Traits.
Defense/Resistance Update

We’re updating how Defense and Resistance work across all units to bring them back in line with their original design intent. Over time, enchantments and hybrid damage types have blurred the distinction between Physical and Magic damage, making traditional tank units less reliable, especially in the late game.

The new system changes how damage reduction is applied, focusing on the source of damage rather than the type of damage dealt. We’re also adding a new Unit Role that deals Magic Damage at Melee range, the Magic Fighter. Several of the existing elemental Fighter and Skirmisher units that we already have will brandish this new Role.
Experience Update

Leveling up units is one of the most rewarding parts of gameplay, but previously, XP gains were heavily tied to combat. This meant players who fought more battles progressed much faster, while others lagged behind. It also made evolving or improving units in the late game difficult, since there were fewer fights available.

All units now gain XP automatically each turn, even when not fighting. This means your armies will continue to improve simply by existing and participating in your empire. XP gained from battles has been halved which means Units still get rewarded for combat, but fighting is no longer the only reliable way to level up. To facilitate all of these changes the XP scale has been increased by a factor 10.

With this we’re also bringing back Exalted Ranks. Once a unit reaches its final rank, it can continue leveling up indefinitely. These extra levels require a large amount of XP, so progression remains slow but rewarding. This system can be disabled through the Advanced Settings for those that desire.
After updating to the Scorpion Beta your in-game version will read 1.014.000.118518.

The most effective way to provide us with feedback is by making a Discussion Thread in the Open Beta Discussions. There’s a couple different types of Feedback that we can process during this Beta period.
Balance

With all of these changes there will naturally be a lot of Balance Feedback. Our goal is to address any extreme imbalances and important feedback that need to be tackled for the Release. We only have time to make these changes until Tuesday the 24th of February.

Balance changes that are more general or require us to change text are not feasible during the Beta Period. This feedback is welcome but will be addressed during our regular development period as resources allow.
Stability
Crashes reported with the Crash Tool will automatically show up in our back end, so when you experience a crash please make sure to Upload those.
If you have a Blocker i.e. a Crash or Hang that will not allow you to continue your game, please make a report and include your Crash Report Name - given after upload - so we can tackle it.
Any general Bugs reported are welcome but not the main focus of this period, we’ll try to address those in a timely manner depending on our available resources.
Modding

If you experience issues and suspect that it might be related to one of the mods you have installed, then please verify which mod it may be by disabling your mods. If you’ve determined which Mod is causing your issue try to contact the Mod Developer first.
If you experience crashes with your mods, then please make a thread as stated above. While outdated mods can cause issues, we do try to ensure that they do not crash.
Rise from Ruin Release
The final Update of this Beta will be when we submit the D0P for Certification. After that the branch will remain active until the release of Rise from Ruin & the Scorpion Update on March 9th.

When the time of release hits the Beta branch will be updated to include the Rise from Ruin Content, this ensures a smooth transition for users switching back to the Default branch. A few hours after release the Scorpion Beta Branch will be disabled and removed. Any remaining users will be automatically moved back to Default when this occurs but it’s advised to switch back yourself after you’ve verified that you have access to the Rise from Ruin content.
